sections.html:
Indiana no longer collects an inheritance tax. The tax applied to people who died on or before December 31, 2012, and lawmakers repealed it in 2013. Heirs who sell a house today owe nothing to the state for the privilege of inheriting it.

The state has also stopped taking returns. No Indiana inheritance tax return should be prepared or filed for a resident or a nonresident, and the old forms are retired. If a question comes up, the Inheritance Tax Division answers at 317-232-2154, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Eastern.

A title company may still ask what applies to a particular deed. For anything about a specific gain, talk to a tax professional or an attorney.

sections.h2: Old inheritance tax language in the Indiana Code
sections.html:
Section 6-4.1-4-0.5 of the Indiana Code still points back to the exemptions in the repealed chapter 6-4.1-3. It does so in the passage that allows an affidavit stating no tax is due.

The same section lets a terminated lien reattach if the state obtains an order that inheritance tax is owed. For a very old death in the family, a title search can turn up this wording. An attorney can tell you whether it touches your file.

The federal estate tax is a separate system run by the IRS, and it reaches only very large estates. A return is due when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, tops the filing threshold for the year of death. A 2025 death uses the 2025 figure even if the house closes in 2026.

Since 2011, the estate of someone survived by a spouse can elect to pass unused exemption to that spouse. The election is made on a timely filed estate tax return.

sections.h2: Taxes when heirs sell an inherited house
sections.html:
An heir who sells is taxed on gain counted from the value at death, not from what the original owner paid. The starting basis is fair market value on the date of death, or the value on the alternate valuation date if the personal representative picks that option.

A gift is the exception. If the heir or the heir's spouse gave appreciated property to the decedent within one year before death, the basis is the decedent's adjusted basis just before death.

  • Ask for the appraisal or the estate's valuation of the house.
  • Save records of repairs and carrying costs paid after the death.
  • Expect Indiana to apply its flat individual rate to any income the federal return reports, as the Indiana capital gains page explains.

sections.h2: When can heirs skip full probate?
sections.html:
For deaths after June 30, 2022, a fiduciary can close a small estate without notice to creditors when the gross probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, is within $100,000 plus administration costs and reasonable funeral expenses. Indiana Code section 29-1-8-3 sets that ceiling.

If the estate holds real property, an affidavit can be recorded with the recorder in the county where the land sits. It must contain:

  • The legal description of the property
  • The dollar threshold that applies to the date of death
  • The name of each person entitled to an interest and the share each receives, divided or undivided
  • A statement explaining how each share was figured

A related rule, section 29-1-8-1, lets distributees collect personal property by affidavit 45 days after death if no one has asked for a personal representative anywhere. It covers things like bank funds, vehicles and securities, not land.

sections.h2: Unsupervised administration and a house sale
sections.html:
Larger estates go through a personal representative. The heirs at law, the legatees and devisees, or the representative can petition the court to let the estate run without court supervision, under Indiana Code 29-1-7.5-1.

After the petition, the clerk issues a notice and the petitioner serves it on the decedent's known creditors. Confirm the representative's power to sell real estate with a probate attorney or the clerk of the county where the case is filed before a listing goes live.

Indiana has 92 counties, and each one handles estate filings through its own clerk. Howard County, for instance, has five courts: a Circuit Court and Superior Courts I through IV. Ask the clerk how filings are routed where your case sits.

sections.h2: Costs that keep running while an estate holds a house
sections.html:
Property tax is billed whether or not the owner has died. Installments fall due in May and November. A payment made within 30 days after the due date on a parcel with no back taxes carries a 5 percent charge, and after that the charge becomes 10 percent of the unpaid tax.

Indiana bills a year behind, so a spring bill after a death often reflects the prior year's ownership. The homestead deduction is renewed only when a property is sold, the title changes or a contract is paid off. Heirs who take title should ask the Howard County Auditor or their own county auditor how the deduction is handled.

Heirs move faster when the file is complete. A short list covers most of it:

  • A certified death certificate and a copy of the will, if there is one
  • Letters from the court, or the affidavit described above if the estate qualifies
  • The deed, the parcel number and the latest property tax bill
  • The date-of-death value, which becomes the starting basis
  • A list of everyone entitled to a share, since the recorded affidavit names each person and each share

See an Indiana probate attorney before anyone signs a deed. The right route depends on the size of the estate and who holds legal authority. A cash buyer can often close once that authority is shown to the title company, which spares heirs months of carrying taxes and insurance on an empty house.

faqs.q: Does Indiana have an estate tax?
faqs.a: Indiana had an inheritance tax, repealed in 2013 for deaths after December 31, 2012. The federal estate tax is separate and has a 2026 filing threshold of $15,000,000.

faqs.q: Do heirs owe Indiana inheritance tax on a house?
faqs.a: No. The state no longer takes inheritance tax returns, and the forms have been retired.

faqs.q: Does an inherited house get a stepped-up basis?
faqs.a: Generally yes. The basis is the fair market value at the date of death, or the alternate valuation date if the personal representative elects it. A gift to the decedent within one year of death is the exception.

faqs.q: How large can an estate be and still use the small estate process?
faqs.a: For deaths after June 30, 2022, the ceiling is $100,000 of gross probate estate after liens and encumbrances, plus administration costs and reasonable funeral expenses. The affidavit for real property is recorded with the county recorder.

faqs.q: Do property taxes stop when the owner dies?
faqs.a: No. Bills keep arriving each May and November, and late payments carry a 5 percent and then a 10 percent charge.
